text: You already know how to pull a year or a month out of a date in SQL. Tableau gives you the same idea through a field menu — but it splits it into two distinct behaviors, and mixing them up is one of the most common beginner mistakes.

Right-click any date field and you'll see a Date Parts section: Year, Quarter, Month, Day. Choosing Month here bins every May together, no matter what year it happened — this is a cyclical grouping that throws the year away entirely.

Just below it sits Date Values: Year 2015, Quarter Q2 2015, Month May 2015, Week Number, Day May 8 2015. Choosing Month here keeps each month tied to its actual year — May 2015 stays separate from May 2016. This is the equivalent of SQL's DATETRUNC. Below both sections sits Exact Date, the full, ungrouped, row-level value.
Next lesson builds directly on this: continuous versus discrete dates, and why that choice is what actually makes a time-series chart look like a trend line instead of a bar chart.
